pr.title: GVN: Support unions.
pr.description:
Supporting union values is not very hard, and allows to const-prop them.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR is a semantics-preserving GVN optimization, not a miscompile fix. The historical pre-PR behavior was a conservative bail-out (`AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(_)) => return None`) that simply failed to const-propagate unions. The new behavior records `Value::Union(active_field, field)` and forwards a projection only when `active == f`; this still reads the same active-field value that the original MIR read. The regression inputs confirm agreement: `union.rs` still drops `un.us == 1`, and `undef_union_as_integer` still transmutes a union whose active field is `()`, yielding undefined bytes in both revisions (and is not a defined concrete execution). The only way to manufacture a differing result would be to model a speculative naive extension that forwards an inactive union field, which is explicitly outside the PR's transformation (`Value::Union(active, field) if active == f`). Thus no source-grounded historically incorrect transformation can be paired against these PR changes.

evidence: +                Value::Union(active, field) if active == f => return Some((projection_ty, field)),
//! Tests that we can propagate into places that are projections into unions
+         _1 = const Union32 {{ value: Indirect { alloc_id: ALLOC0, offset: Size(0 bytes) }: u32, unit: () }};
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical behavior was conservative bail-out rather than a wrong rewrite: GVN returned `None` for union aggregates, so it missed the const-propagation opportunity and left the union construction plus active-field copy intact. The new correct transformation records `Value::Union(active_field, field)` and rewrites only a matching active-field projection; the supplied diff shows `_1 = Un { us: move _2 };` becoming `_1 = const Un {{ us: 1_u32 }};` and `_4 = copy (_1.0: u32);` becoming `_4 = const 1_u32;`. A naive extension that forwarded any union field, rather than only the active one, would exceed the supported domain.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing a union aggregate `AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(active_field))` with one field operand, followed by `ProjectionElem::Field(f, _)` on that same union value. For actual constant evaluation, the union type must also have `BackendRepr::Scalar(..)` or `BackendRepr::ScalarPair(..)`; any other backend representation is outside the supported constant-folding domain. Reads of a field other than the active field are outside the forwarding domain.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, GVN deliberately refused to track unions. The aggregate handler had `// Do not track unions.` followed by `AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(_)) => return None`, and field projection only forwarded reads from `Value::Aggregate` or from a downcast projection. Consequently a union construction such as `_1 = Un { us: move _2 };` and a later `_4 = copy (_1.0: u32);` remained unfurled rather than becoming a constant union and a constant field read.
pitfalls: Only the active union field may be forwarded: the patch guards with `Value::Union(active, field) if active == f`. Forwarding a different field would treat a union reinterpretation/read as if it were an aggregate field read.
Const evaluation must bail out for non-scalar, non-scalar-pair union layouts, as shown by `return None;` after the backend-repr match.

A zero-sized or unit active field does not initialize the whole union allocation. The `undef_union_as_integer` test preserves an uninitialized u32: the union constant is `Union32 {{ value: Indirect { alloc_id: ALLOC0, offset: Size(0 bytes) }: u32, unit: () }}` and ALLOC0 is rendered `__ __ __ __ │ ░░░░`; do not assume zeroed bytes.
Union aggregates carry a single field operand, so the implementation uses `fields.first()?` rather than indexing a full field list.
Do not conflate the pre-existing downcast guard `written_variant == read_variant` with union field selection; they are separate conditions in the projection match.

The old DestinationPropagation union diffs becoming empty does not by itself prove anything about DestinationPropagation correctness; the test was moved to `tests/mir-opt/const_prop/union.rs` and repurposed for GVN.
preconditions: GVN sees an `AggregateKind::Adt(_, _, _, _, Some(active_field))` union construction with at least one field operand; the patch uses `let field = *fields.first()?;`.
The projection being forwarded is `ProjectionElem::Field(f, _)` on a `Value::Union(active, field)` and only when `active == f`.
Constant evaluation of the union is attempted only when `matches!(ty.backend_repr, BackendRepr::Scalar(..) | BackendRepr::ScalarPair(..))`.
The constant-evaluation path allocates `MemoryKind::Stack`, projects the active field, copies the field into it, and marks the allocation immutable; failure at any step returns `None`.
analysis.summary: GVN gained a Value::Union(active_field, field) representation so union aggregate constructions can be hash-consed and reads of the active field forwarded, letting unions be const-propagated when their layout is Scalar or ScalarPair. This was a performance/optimization extension, not a confirmed miscompile fix.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt test with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir` emitting `union.main.GVN.diff`. Construct a union whose active field comes from a function returning a constant, then read that same field; assert the union construction becomes `const Un {{{{ us: 1_u32 }}}}` and the field read becomes a constant, as the new test does with `// CHECK: [[un]] = const Un {{{{ us: 1_u32 }}}};`. Also test the uninitialized-byte edge case using a union with a unit active field transmuted to an integer (`undef_union_as_integer`), checking `_1 = const Union32` and an undefined ALLOC0 (`__ __ __ __`), including 32-bit and 64-bit variants. Compare the before/after GVN diff to ensure only the intended active-field reads are forwarded.
analysis.trigger: A union value is constructed from a field operand and a later field projection reads the active field, especially after MIR inlining. The added test uses a `union Un { us: u32 }`, builds it with `Un { us: val() }`, and reads `un.us`; with GVN the union becomes `const Un {{ us: 1_u32 }}` and the projection becomes `const 1_u32`.
